# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The `AppLayout` component establishes clean HTML5 landmark regions, logical heading structure, and accessible naming. However, it suffers from two major accessibility design defects in focus management: 1. **Positive `tabIndex={1}` on the Floating Action Button (`.fab`)**, which hijacks the sequential navigation flow and forces keyboard focus to the floating button before any other element on the page (even before the skip link). 2. **Visual vs. DOM order mismatch caused by CSS flexbox `order: -1` on `.sidebar`**, causing keyboard navigation to visit the main content before the sidebar navigation, directly contradicting the visual presentation (sidebar on the left, main content on the right). 3. **Broken skip link target programmatics (`
`)**, where in modern browsers clicking an in-page anchor to a container element without `tabIndex={-1}` fails to move keyboard focus to that element. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions - Positive `tabIndex` breaking sequential navigation flow. - CSS layout manipulation (`order: -1` or `flex-direction: row-reverse`) decoupling visual order from DOM tab order. - In-page skip link anchor failing to shift keyboard focus due to missing `tabindex="-1"`. - Focus indicators having insufficient contrast or being obscured by sticky/fixed elements (FAB or header). --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (blocks or severely breaks navigation access) 1. **Positive `tabIndex={1}` Hijacks Page Tab Order** - **Location**: `AppLayout.jsx:81` - **Element**: `` - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users. - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. - **Fix**: Wrap the visible text symbol in `+` so screen readers do not announce "plus" alongside the accessible name on certain AT/browser combinations. 2. **Missing `aria-current="page"` on Active Navigation Links** - **Location**: `AppLayout.jsx:68` - **Element**: `
  • Dashboard
    • ` - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users, Cognitive accessibility users. - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. - **Fix**: Indicate the currently active view programmatically using `aria-current="page"`. --- ## Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | **MEDIUM** | Skip target missing programmatic focusability; missing `aria-current` | | Keyboard-only | **HIGH** | Positive `tabIndex={1}`; CSS flex `order: -1` visual inversion | | Low vision | **MEDIUM** | Sidebar link focus ring contrast fails 3:1 (`#a8d0f0` on `#f8fafc`) | | Cognitive | **LOW** | Logical layout, consistent structure | | Vestibular & motion | **LOW** | No animations or auto-play | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No audio/video content | | Environmental contrast | **MEDIUM** | Focus indicator contrast in sidebar | --- ## What's Missing - **Programmatic focus target on main container**: `
    ` to capture focus on skip-link activation. - **Active item state**: `aria-current="page"` on current navigation entries in header/sidebar. - **Visual hiding for decorative characters**: `aria-hidden="true"` on the `+` inside the floating action button. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen Reader User**: Landmarks (`
    `, `
    `, `
    `, `
    `) and section labelling via `aria-labelledby` are well implemented. However, navigating sequentially will follow the unexpected order: Skip Link → Header → Main Content → Sidebar → FAB. - **Keyboard-only User**: The experience is heavily impaired. On page load, `Tab` jumps immediately to the bottom-right FAB due to `tabIndex={1}`. Once past the header, tabbing enters the main body on the right side of the screen before jumping back to the sidebar on the left. - **Low Vision User**: Tracking the focus ring through the sidebar is difficult due to `#a8d0f0` failing contrast against `#f8fafc`. Jumping from main content backwards to the sidebar creates cognitive disorientation at high zoom levels. - **Cognitive Accessibility**: Clean and structured headings, but the jumpy tab sequence is disorienting. --- ## Verdict Justification The layout has solid semantic foundations, but the presence of a positive `tabIndex` (`tabIndex={1}`), visual/DOM order inversion via CSS `order: -1`, and non-focusable skip-link target make it an unacceptable keyboard experience in its current state. **Requirements for upgrade to ACCEPT**: 1. Remove `tabIndex={1}` from the FAB. 2. Align DOM order with visual order by placing `
    ` before `
    ` and dropping `order: -1`. 3. Put `id="content"` and `tabIndex={-1}` directly on `
    `. 4. Increase sidebar focus outline contrast to `>= 3:1`.
